issues.description: Basic usage example accesses node with `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` which is brittle and stylistically poor
issues.detail: The line `training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` but obscures intent and could mislead readers about Pipeline API. A clearer pattern would be `pipeline.nodes[0]` or filtering by name (`training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes if n.name == 'train_model_node')`). For introductory documentation, brittleness in the canonical example matters.

issues.description: Mermaid example uses unreachable/dead code after `return`
issues.detail: In the Image preview example, a commented-out `return ImagePreview(...)` is shown after a live `return`. This is fine as comments, but the surrounding text says 'Or a data URI for inline images' without explaining that you must replace, not append. Beginners may copy-paste both blocks and be confused that the second `return` is unreachable. Clarify that these are alternatives.

issues.description: Inconsistent/incomplete `node(...)` snippets that won't run as written
issues.detail: Several illustrative snippets (e.g., the Mermaid `node(func=process_data, ...)` block, the Text preview `node(func=calculate_metrics, ...)` block, and the closure example) appear at module top level without being wrapped in a Pipeline and reference undefined functions (`process_data`, `calculate_metrics`). Readers who copy-paste will get NameErrors. Either mark these as 'illustrative only' or wrap them in a runnable Pipeline as the Basic usage example does.

issues.description: Contradictory guidance about preview function access to data context
issues.detail: The 'Using preview functions with data context' section says 'Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs directly... If you need to generate previews based on actual data, you can use closures or access datasets within the preview function.' The second clause ('access datasets within the preview function') is mentioned but not demonstrated, and could imply DataCatalog access inside preview_fn which has different lifecycle/threading implications. Either show the dataset-access pattern explicitly or drop that phrase.
issues.lines: Using preview functions with data context

issues.description: Mermaid `securityLevel: 'strict'` shown as example may break user diagrams
issues.detail: The example sets `securityLevel: 'strict'` which disables click handlers and HTML labels in Mermaid. The comment lists 'strict, loose, antiscript' as options without warning that 'strict' is more restrictive than Mermaid's default ('strict' in older versions, but functionality-wise it sandboxes more). A canonical doc example shouldn't default users into the most restrictive setting without explaining the trade-off, or should use Mermaid's default.

issues.description: Best practice 5 ('Handle errors: Wrap preview logic in try-except if needed') is vague and potentially misleading
issues.detail: This advice is too thin to be actionable: what should the function return on failure? If preview_fn raises, does node.preview() propagate, return None, or return an error preview? The doc should specify the contract for failure or show a concrete pattern (e.g., returning `TextPreview(content=f'Preview failed: {e}')`). Without this, users will write inconsistent error handling that the Viz frontend may not handle well.

issues.description: PR checklist explicitly admits no tests and no RELEASE.md entry
issues.detail: While this is a docs-only PR (so tests may be N/A), the absence of a RELEASE.md entry is a process gap given the user-facing feature being documented is new and experimental. The experimental warning is good, but downstream users tracking releases won't find the docs cross-referenced. Add a RELEASE.md note pointing to the new section.

issues.description: Adding lowercase 'polars' to ignore.txt duplicates 'Polars' and may mask real misspellings
issues.detail: ignore.txt already contains 'Polars'. Vale typically handles case-insensitively or via case-sensitive rules; adding both 'Polars' and 'polars' suggests the underlying rule is case-sensitive. Worth a one-line comment explaining why both forms are needed, otherwise future maintainers will deduplicate it.

issues.description: Heading 'JSON preview' added to headings.yml exceptions but other acronyms used in headings aren't
issues.detail: Adding 'JSON' to headings.yml is consistent with existing entries (YAML, etc.). However, the new section also uses 'Plotly preview', 'Mermaid preview' as headings — those proper nouns are presumably already allowed. Minor: confirm no other new headings need exception entries (e.g., if any heading were 'API preview' or similar).

'Preview function enables you to inject a callable which helps in debugging and monitoring.' should be 'Preview functions enable...' (plural agreement with intro). 'Serialise' is British English; rest of doc mixes 'visualisation' (BR) and 'visualization' is not used, but check Kedro's style guide for consistency. Double space after 'described in' before the experimental.md link.

issues.description: Docstring example in TextPreview uses `\"\"\"` escaping that may render oddly
issues.detail: The `generate_code_preview` example has `\"\"\"Calculate key performance metrics.\"\"\"` inside a Python triple-quoted string. While syntactically valid, rendering this through a doc site code block may produce literal backslashes depending on the markdown renderer. Worth verifying the rendered output on the docs site.

issues.description: Mermaid example label 'Training Samples: 10,000' uses commas inside brackets
issues.detail: Mermaid node labels with commas and colons inside `[...]` brackets can sometimes confuse parsers without quoting. The example may render but is on the edge of safe Mermaid syntax. Consider quoting: `C["Training Samples: 10,000"]`. Low risk if you've tested it on Kedro-Viz's Mermaid version.

issues.description: No link to API reference for `preview_fn` / `PreviewContract` classes
issues.detail: The docs reference `JsonPreview`, `TablePreview`, etc., but never link to autogenerated API reference for `kedro.pipeline.preview_contract`. Adding a 'See API reference' link at the end of 'Available preview types' would help users discover constructor signatures and the exact `to_dict()` contract.

issues.description: 'For a complete list of available Mermaid configuration options' links to external Mermaid schema docs without pinning
issues.detail: External docs links rot. Kedro-Viz merges this config with defaults, so the relevant surface is whatever Kedro-Viz supports — not the entire Mermaid schema. Consider linking to a Kedro-Viz-specific config reference, or note 'subject to what Kedro-Viz's embedded Mermaid version supports'.

dissents.topic: Whether the doc should show a fully runnable end-to-end example or accept illustrative snippets

positions.position: Docs are read non-linearly; illustrative `node(...)` blocks with undefined `process_data` are fine because the Basic usage section already shows a complete Pipeline. Demanding every snippet be runnable bloats docs.

Every code block in user-facing docs should be copy-paste runnable or clearly marked '# illustrative — define process_data first'. Otherwise the doc fails the 'getting started' contract and produces avoidable NameErrors during onboarding.

dissents.topic: How strict to be on experimental-feature documentation

positions.position: The experimental warning at top is sufficient. Detailing failure modes, contract, and edge cases now is premature when the API may change.

Experimental features deserve *more* documentation of contract (what preview_fn signature is allowed, what happens on exception, threading guarantees, when it's invoked), not less, because early adopters will lock in usage patterns that are hard to migrate later.

dissents.topic: Whether adding lowercase 'polars' to ignore.txt is a real issue

positions.position: Duplicating 'Polars' and 'polars' indicates the linter rule is case-sensitive; both entries are correct because the doc legitimately uses both forms (proper noun and code identifier). No issue.
Without a comment, the duplication will be 'cleaned up' by a future contributor. Either add a comment or fix the underlying Vale rule to be case-insensitive.

review.summary: This is a docs-only PR adding a substantial new section for the experimental Node Preview feature, plus two small Vale linter adjustments. The writing is clear and well-structured, with appropriate experimental-warning placement and good coverage of all preview types. The main concerns are: (1) several code snippets reference undefined functions or aren't wrapped in runnable Pipelines, which will frustrate copy-paste users; (2) the contract for `preview_fn` (exception handling, data-context access, signature constraints) is under-specified for an experimental API where early adopters will set patterns; (3) minor stylistic and accuracy nits in Mermaid examples, error-handling guidance, and external links. No P0 blockers — this is safe to merge after addressing the runnable-snippet and contract-clarity items.
